text: Long ago, in the year 1900, a baby girl was born in Padang Panjang, a town in the green mountains of West Sumatra, in what is now Indonesia. Her name was Rahmah.
Her family loved learning. Her father was a judge, and her grandfather was a scholar who studied the stars.
Her people, the Minangkabau, build beautiful houses with roofs that curve up like the horns of a buffalo.
Find the pairs! Things of her home in the mountains.
Where was Rahmah born?
In the mountains of Sumatra
In a big desert
She was born in Padang Panjang, in the green mountains of West Sumatra.
When Rahmah was six years old, her father died. She missed him very much.
But her father's students came to teach her. She learned to read and write, in Arabic letters and in Latin letters too.
Count the books she read! Tap each one.
She also learned how to help mothers when their babies are born.
Who taught Rahmah after her father died?
Nobody at all
Her father's students
Her father's students came and taught her to read and write.
When Rahmah was still very young, her family arranged for her to marry, and she had to leave school.
But Rahmah did not stop learning. She joined study circles, where women sat together in the evening to learn about Islam.
Keep learning, like Rahmah. Press and hold.
A few years later, she went back to school.
What did Rahmah do when she had to leave school?
She kept learning
She stopped learning
She kept learning, in study circles, until she could go back to school.
Her big brother, Zainuddin, had started a school called Diniyah. Rahmah went back there to study.
After class, she gathered the girls together, to study more.
Count the girls in her study circle. Tap each one.
She saw that girls needed a school of their own, where they could learn everything, and feel at home.
What did Rahmah want for girls?
No school at all
A school of their own
She wanted girls to have a school of their own.
On the first of November, 1923, Rahmah opened a school just for girls. She called it Diniyah Putri.
At first there was no school building. Lessons were in a mosque, and Rahmah was the main teacher.
The first students were seventy-one women and girls. Many of them were young mothers.

Where were the very first lessons?
In a mosque
In a palace
The first lessons were in a mosque.
Not everyone liked the new school. Some people said that girls did not need to go to school.
Rahmah talked kindly with the scholars of her town, and showed them that Islam honours learning, for girls as well as boys.
Then, in 1924, her brother Zainuddin died. Many thought the school would close. But Rahmah kept going.

She gave up

She kept going, and the school did not close.
In 1926, a big earthquake shook Padang Panjang, and the school building fell down.
But the lessons did not stop. For years, the girls learned in simple shelters.
Rahmah travelled to many towns and islands, to collect money for a new school.
Help Rahmah travel to collect money for the school.
In 1928, the new school opened!
Build the new school. Tap to place every brick.
In those days the land was ruled by the Dutch, and their government paid money to some schools. But Rahmah would not take it: she wanted her school to be free to teach in its own way.
The school grew and grew. Soon about five hundred girls were learning there.
She also opened a college to train women to be teachers.

Think again. Would a good teacher do that?
For many years, Indonesia was ruled by others. Then, in 1945, Indonesia became free.
When Rahmah heard the news, she raised the red and white flag of Indonesia in the school yard.
Raise the flag! Press and hold.
What colours are on Indonesia's flag?
Red and white
Blue and yellow
Indonesia's flag is red and white.
Years later, the head of al-Azhar, a great old university in Egypt, came all the way to visit her school.
Then Rahmah went on Hajj to Makkah.
Help Rahmah travel to Makkah, and then to Cairo.
In Cairo, the teachers of al-Azhar gave her the title Syaikhah: a great scholar. No woman had ever been given it before.
After that, girls from her school could go to study at al-Azhar too.
What title did al-Azhar give Rahmah?
Queen
Syaikhah: a great scholar
Al-Azhar called her Syaikhah, a great scholar. No woman had been given it before.
Rahmah never stopped working. In 1967, a university for women, which she had worked for, was opened.
Rahmah died in 1969, in Padang Panjang, where she was born. May Allah have mercy on her.
Her school is still open today, full of girls learning.
And in 2025, Indonesia named her a National Hero.
Tell Rahmah's story. Tap in order.
First, Rahmah was born in the mountains of Sumatra.
She learned to read and write.
She opened a school for girls.
An earthquake knocked it down, and she built it again.
She raised Indonesia's flag at the school.
And al-Azhar called her Syaikhah.
Listen again, and tell it in order.
This is the story of Rahmah El Yunusiyyah, who opened a school for girls when many people said girls did not need one, and never gave up. Her school is still open today.
